evidence: Parent Approach: 'Each child collapses one duplicated computation into one shared module ... and lands with a construct-uniqueness guard.'

1dd5 AC: 'A bug fix touching a file with ≥2 bug-trailer commits in the prior 7 days is escalated ...' — a NEW observable behaviour.
2e0f AC: 'The five cited src-only diff shapes select the tests overlay ...' — a NEW observable behaviour.

findings.finding: Nine children (1dd5, 2e0f, 4144, 73b8, 77e7, 7f54, a4d7, d075, dff2) contradict the parent's stated Approach and are not reflected in the parent's Acceptance Criteria or Child-responsibilities list. The parent Approach asserts 'Each child collapses one duplicated computation into one shared module, keeps every current behaviour pinned by the tests named in the child, and lands with a construct-uniqueness guard.' These nine children have no shared module, no construct-uniqueness guard, and (for the skill/gate children) deliberately CHANGE observable behaviour — directly conflicting with parent AC2 ('No child changes an observable behaviour').
scenarios: The epic completion verifier applies parent AC2's rule ('no child changes an observable behaviour') to 1dd5/2e0f/4144/77e7/7f54 and reports them as violations, because those children intentionally introduce new blocking/validation/carry-forward behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Either split the behaviour-changing children into a separate epic, or amend the parent Approach/AC2 to scope 'no observable-behaviour change' and 'construct-uniqueness guard' to the consolidation children only and enumerate the behaviour-adding children as an explicit exception.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile parent AC3 (net-negative non-test LOC) with the additive policy/skill/tooling children by either scoping AC3 to the consolidation children only or naming the offsetting deletions.
evidence: Parent AC3: 'The net non-test line count across the epic's landed changes is negative; checked by summing `git show --numstat` over the children's trailer commits.'
Parent Approach: 'Each child collapses one duplicated computation into one shared module' — the nine children named do not.

Only 1cf6, 7931, da84 individually assert a negative/at-least-negative net LOC; the additive children assert none and are net-positive by construction (new predicate, new trigger, new doc, new validation, new schema field, new carry-forward).
findings.finding: Parent AC3 ('the net non-test line count across the epic's landed changes is negative; checked by summing git show --numstat over the children's trailer commits') is threatened by nine children that are purely additive and collapse no duplicated computation. 1dd5 adds a new escalation predicate + backtest extension; 2e0f adds a content trigger; 4144 adds routing entries + a replay doc; 73b8 adds tooling/backlog fixes; 77e7 adds validation + a schema field + fsck check; 7f54 adds carry-forward logic; a4d7/d075/dff2 add skill/doc prose. These add lines without the compensating deletions the consolidation children provide, so the epic-wide sum is not structurally guaranteed to be negative.
scenarios: The 14 consolidation children land net-negative, but the nine additive children add enough lines that the summed `git show --numstat` over ALL children's trailer commits is non-negative, failing the epic completion verifier for AC3.
findings.suggested_fix: State in AC3 whether the sum is over the consolidation children only, or exempt the additive children explicitly; otherwise the epic verifier is structurally guaranteed to be at risk.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Constrain the step-4 def-count fallback: require the child to justify that no distinctive atom/AST shape exists, and state that a def-count guard does not catch inline/aliased re-duplication (bound or eliminate this residual so no child silently ships a weaker guard).
evidence: Plan step 4: 'Where the construct has no distinctive atoms, assert the definition count of the named symbol instead (exactly one `def <name>` under `src/rebar`).'

Exemplar rationale (test_spawn_detached.py:44-46): 'a fourth copy-pasted site that no test happens to execute must still fail here. This is what makes the consolidation durable' — a def-count check does NOT catch an inline/aliased copy-paste, only a second literal `def`.
Step 2 already prefers atom-conjunction/AST matching precisely because a single common token is too weak; step 4 reintroduces a single-shape (def keyword) match.
findings.finding: The Guard-test construction rule step 4 fallback ('assert the definition count of the named symbol ... exactly one `def <name>` under src/rebar') is a materially weaker mechanism than the atom-conjunction/AST-shape guard for the epic's own target failure mode: a re-duplication pasted as inline code, an aliased/wrapped def, or a lambda has no matching `def <name>` and passes the count assertion, so the twin re-enters silently — the exact 'copy lands, guard misses it' failure the exemplar's static-atom scan was built to prevent. The plan invokes this fallback 'where the construct has no distinctive atoms' without bounding when a child may use it or acknowledging the residual.
scenarios: A child whose construct step 4 deems atom-less lands a def-count guard; a later change re-inlines the logic at a call site (no new `def`), the count stays 1, the guard passes, and the twin-divergence class the epic set out to close reopens undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 4 that the fallback is permitted only after a child documents why no distinctive atom or AST call-shape exists, and pair the def-count assertion with a call-site or AST-shape scan wherever the construct is invoked (not merely defined), so an inline re-duplication still fires.
